QUIC and UDP benchmark tile with socket setup, packet forwarding, and AIO TX handling.

# Purpose
This file defines the `benchs` tile for the `fd_topo` runtime. It sets up a packet forwarding and QUIC client benchmark path that can run in two modes: raw UDP send mode when `no_quic` is set, and QUIC client mode when QUIC is enabled. The code allocates and initializes the tile context, opens and binds UDP sockets, connects them to the target address and port, and prepares the scratch memory needed for the tile and for the QUIC engine.

The file also defines the tile callbacks used by the `stem` execution loop. [`before_frag`](<#before_frag>) updates the current time and selects work by round robin. [`during_frag`](<#during_frag>) sends packets either directly with `send()` or through the QUIC stack by creating connections and streams, then passing packet data to `fd_quic_stream_send()`. The QUIC path also services socket input with `poll()` and `recvmmsg()`, rebuilds the IP and UDP header fields expected by `fd_quic_process_packet()`, and flushes outgoing QUIC packets through an `fd_aio_t` transmit callback that strips the IP and UDP headers before calling `sendmmsg()`. The file ends by exporting `fd_tile_benchs`, which registers the tile name, memory layout functions, init functions, and run function for the topology system.
